transcript.text: This is Swift, an automated flood assistant working with local emergency services. Am I speaking with someone at 1868 Gretna Green Drive?
Yes, this is me. My wife’s recovering from surgery and can’t walk. Water’s already in the house.
Thank you for confirming your situation. How many people are at the home right now, including anyone who can't come to the phone?
One person here, my wife’s recovering from surgery and can’t walk.

I hear you’re caring for someone who can’t walk right now. Is there anyone there who can't leave on their own, for example someone who uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound? If it's a wheelchair, does it have a motor?
Yes, my wife can’t walk—she’s recovering from surgery. No wheelchair, motor or not.
I hear you’re caring for your wife during recovery. Is there water inside the home right now?
Yes, water’s inside. She can’t walk—need help.
I hear you’re in trouble. Stay put and wait for help. If neighbors need a ride out, do you have a high-clearance truck, a boat, or free seats in a vehicle?
No truck, no boat, no seats. My wife can’t walk—she’s recovering from surgery.
I hear you’re without transport or seating options right now. Let me read that back: 1 people; wife needs help leaving because of recovering from surgery; water is inside. Is that right?
Yes. Wife can’t walk. Water’s in. No truck or boat.

Thank you for confirming your situation. I've recorded that you need help leaving. No responder has been assigned yet. If water is rising inside, move to the highest floor and call 911 if you can get through. Goodbye.

house_card: Two people. Wife can’t leave—recovering from surgery. Water inside. English.
